claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a single-phase refractory structure.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr retains high strength from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
Replacing part of Mo with an equivalent atomic amount of Al will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed Mo-to-Al substitution is represented as HfMo(1−x)AlxTaTiZr with 0 < x ≤ 0.1.
The Al-modified alloy will retain a single-phase solid-solution matrix that is body-centered cubic or structurally similar.
The combination of transition metals and Al stabilizes the proposed single-phase matrix.
Al is lighter than Mo and therefore lowers alloy density when it substitutes for Mo.
Al acts as a larger atom in this alloy and introduces additional atomic-scale lattice distortion.
The additional lattice distortion produces solid-solution strengthening.
Solid-solution strengthening from Al substitution will maintain mechanical strength at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
Relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, the modified alloy's density will decrease by up to a few percent.
Relative to the baseline, yield strength and hardness will remain comparable or become slightly higher at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is intended to apply up to approximately 10 at.% Al, at temperatures up to 1000 °C, under moderate strain rates near 10^−3 s^−1 and in vacuum or a protective atmosphere.
Excessive Al additions or temperatures above 1000 °C may cause phase instability or oxidation.
The Al solubility limit and its effect on high-temperature phase stability in this alloy are not fully established, and phase separation could impair mechanical properties.

The hypothesis is rejected if an Al-containing alloy fails to achieve more than a 1% density reduction or loses more than 10% yield strength at either room temperature or the designated high temperature.

contradictions.description: The formula HfMo(1−x)AlxTaTiZr with x ≤ 0.1 gives at most about 2 at.% Al because the formula contains five total atomic units. The boundary instead describes the intervention as extending to approximately 10 at.% Al. Thus x = 0.1 and 10 at.% Al are not equivalent composition limits.
